constraints: ContextRequirement describes semantic need, source constraints and hard limits only; strict parsing rejects provider/tool commands and lifecycle-authority fields.
ContextResolution binds exact requirement identity, exact source snapshots/currentness validators, provenance, materialization identity, unresolved evidence and immutable progression.
Current Backend repository and QA accepted-artifact context must map into the same contract without weakening exact revision, sourceRef, producer or acceptance-decision provenance.
Core must not import Oracle. Core receives opaque JSON-safe requirement/resolution values only through an injected pre-render resolver port.
Selected ContextRequirement blocks resolve once per AgentRuntime call before prompt rendering; turn-aware strategies reuse that exact resolved projection across turns.
Required missing, stale, ambiguous, unverifiable-currentness or budget-exhausted evidence yields UNSATISFIED and prevents model generation; optional unresolved evidence is explicit PARTIAL.
Currentness is not timestamp freshness: REQUIRED CURRENT evidence must bind an exact snapshotRef plus at least one strong validator.
Worker execution remains unauthorized until researchGaps are empty and a new exact Jev readiness judgment is SATISFIED.
invariants: Application/domain controllers own work semantics, acceptance, publication, recovery and product authority; Oracle only resolves context.
Every ContextResolution is bounded by explicit requirement/budget and preserves source provenance/currentness; missing or ambiguous required evidence fails closed.
Oracle is infrastructure-owned and provider/planner internals do not become model-visible scheduling authority or Core/Application implementation ownership.
architectureDecisions: D1 — ContextRequirement v1 is provider-neutral and strict: consumerRef, semanticNeed, ordered evidence requirements and a hard budget; unknown provider/tool/lifecycle fields are rejected.
D2 — Each evidence requirement has id, necessity REQUIRED|OPTIONAL, semantic need, source kind/ref, EXACT|CURRENT snapshot constraint, optional itemRefs and requiredProvenance constraints.
D3 — requirementId = SHA-256 of canonical semantic requirement fields excluding requirementId itself; evidence order is semantic and duplicate evidence ids are invalid.

D4 — ContextResolution v1 contains requirementId, immutable step parent/index, COMPLETE|PARTIAL|UNSATISFIED status, normalized items, explicit unresolved evidence, materialization identity and cumulative budget consumption.

D5 — itemDigest binds source snapshot, currentness validators, provenance and content; materialization.id binds normalized ordered items; resolutionId binds requirementId + step + status + materialization.id + unresolved state.
D6 — Provider calls, latency and consumed counters are operational evidence and do not enter resolutionId; different provider implementations may produce the same semantic resolution.

D7 — COMPLETE means all required and optional evidence is resolved; PARTIAL means all required evidence is resolved with optional evidence explicitly unresolved; UNSATISFIED means at least one required evidence requirement is unresolved and is non-consumable.

D8 — REQUIRED CURRENT evidence must resolve to an exact snapshotRef plus at least one STRONG validator. Modification timestamps may be retained as weak evidence but cannot alone satisfy REQUIRED CURRENT.

D9 — Provenance is typed lineage evidence, not authority. Producer work-order, acceptance-decision and artifact-manifest refs can constrain/describe resolution but cannot confer acceptance/publication/recovery rights.

D10 — Budget v1 uses maxItems, maxMaterializedBytes, maxProviderCalls and maxResolutionSteps. Token budget is deferred because tokenization is model-specific; Core separately preserves maxSerializedChars.
D11 — Progressive resolution is explicit immutable chaining: index starts at 0, previousResolutionId is exact, cumulative consumption never decreases, and no step mutates a prior resolution in place.
D12 — The semantic schema implementation belongs under @exharness/oracle. No shared contracts package is introduced; Core does not import Oracle or duplicate Oracle schema.

D13 — Core adds contextRequirementBlocks + contextResolver as a generic pre-render port. A selected block resolves exactly once per agent call, projects to an ordinary fixed context block, then existing renderAgentContext enforces trust and serialized-size policy.
D14 — Requirement-resolution failure or projection rejection occurs before model generation. Capability, Resource and LiveObject invocation counts remain zero for context resolution.
D15 — Backend/QA compatibility is proven by deterministic fixture mappers only in BB-061; production provider orchestration remains unchanged until later Oracle tasks.
implementationSlices: S1 [CONTRACT,IDENTITY,INV-2] — Add packages/oracle/src/context-contract.js and export it from packages/oracle/src/index.js. Implement strict JSON-safe parsers/constructors for ContextRequirement v1 and ContextResolution v1 plus SHA-256 helpers contextRequirementId(), contextItemDigest(), contextMaterializationId(), contextResolutionId() and assertConsumableContextResolution(). Reject unknown fields at every semantic object level. requirementId hashes every semantic requirement field except itself; itemDigest binds source snapshot/currentness/provenance/content; materialization id binds normalized ordered items; resolutionId binds requirementId + step + status + materialization id + unresolved state and excludes cost/timing counters.

S2 [CURRENTNESS,BUDGET,PROGRESSION,INV-2] — Enforce REQUIRED|OPTIONAL coverage, EXACT|CURRENT source constraints, requiredProvenance matching, hard maxItems/maxMaterializedBytes/maxProviderCalls/maxResolutionSteps, explicit unresolved reasons, COMPLETE/PARTIAL/UNSATISFIED status, strong-validator requirement for REQUIRED CURRENT, and immutable progression {index,previousResolutionId}. Cumulative counters may not decrease or exceed the original requirement budget. UNSATISFIED is non-consumable; PARTIAL is consumable only when every REQUIRED evidence need is satisfied.

S3 [CORE_PORT,INV-3] — Add packages/core-harness/src/context-resolution.js with defineContextRequirementBlock() and resolveContextRequirementBlocks(). Core treats requirement/resolution values as opaque JSON-safe data. A requirement block is {name,description?,trust,requirement,project}. resolveContextRequirementBlocks receives selected block names, resolver.resolve(requirement,metadata), and returns ordinary fixed ContextBlock definitions. Core imports no Oracle module.

S4 [RUNTIME_PATH,FAIL_CLOSED,INV-3] — Extend createAgentRuntime() with contextRequirementBlocks=[] and contextResolver=null. For each run, after callId/input/context are established and before any prompt render/model generation, resolve selected requirement blocks exactly once using metadata {callId,judgment,input,context}; project each resolution; combine projected fixed blocks with existing ordinary context blocks; then call existing renderAgentContext. Turn-aware prepareTurn() re-renders ordinary context/history but reuses the same fixed projected requirement blocks for every turn in that call. Unselected requirement blocks cause zero resolver calls. Missing resolver, resolver rejection or project rejection fails before model generation and without Capability/Resource/LiveObject invocation.

S5 [COMPATIBILITY,INV-1] — Add scripts/oracle-context-intelligence/bb061-contract-compatibility-probe.mjs using deterministic fixtures only. Map one current BackendWorkOrder into repository EXACT requirements and one current QaWorkOrder into accepted-artifact EXACT requirements with required producer/acceptance provenance; construct fixture ContextResolutions; map back through existing BackendContextSchema/QaContextSchema. Assert exact repository ref/revision/file ordering/sourceRef and exact QA upstream/artifact/sourceRef/APPLICATION_ARTIFACT producer+acceptance provenance survive. Do not change Backend/QA production application paths.

S6 [VERIFICATION,AUTHORITY] — Add packages/oracle/test/context-contract.test.js, packages/core-harness/test/context-resolution.test.js and test/oracle-context-contract-boundary.test.mjs. Cover every identity field, unknown/provider/tool/lifecycle fields, stale/weak-only CURRENT, missing/ambiguous/budget exhaustion, optional partial, progression parent/index/counters, provenance identity, same semantic result under different operational cost, no Core->Oracle import, no Oracle lifecycle authority, once-per-call resolution and zero model/action calls on failure.

S7 [LIVING_TRUTH] — Update Oracle Living architecture/state/semantics with the delivered semantic contract and explicit limits; update Core architecture/state/workflow with the injected pre-render context-resolution port, once-per-call freeze semantics and separation from Capability/Resource/LiveObject. Do not claim provider catalog/planner, durable resolution persistence/cache invalidation, automatic progressive re-resolution or benchmark value.

negativeVerificationCases: ContextRequirement accepts providerId/tool/operation/queryDsl/mcpMethod, task lifecycle commands, acceptance/publication/recovery directives or any other unknown semantic field.
A REQUIRED CURRENT item has only weak/timestamp currentness evidence or no exact snapshotRef but is treated as consumable.
A required evidence need is missing/stale/ambiguous/budget-exhausted yet resolution status is COMPLETE or PARTIAL.
Optional unresolved evidence disappears instead of producing explicit PARTIAL + unresolved reason.
Operational provider calls/latency change resolutionId for otherwise identical semantic materialization.
A later progressive resolution rewrites an earlier resolution, skips the exact parent, decrements cumulative consumption or exceeds the original budget.
Core imports @exharness/oracle or interprets provider/source-specific fields instead of treating requirement/resolution as opaque JSON-safe data.
A selected requirement block resolves more than once in a single turn-aware agent call, causing hidden context drift.
Resolver/project failure still reaches the model or increments Capability/Resource/LiveObject invocation.
Backend/QA compatibility mapping drops exact revision/sourceRef/producer/acceptance-decision provenance.
Living Docs claim provider catalog/planner, durable resolution storage/cache invalidation, automatic progressive resolution or benchmark value is delivered by BB-061.

requirement.identity: requirementId = sha256(canonical(all semantic fields except requirementId))
requirement.strictness: Unknown fields are rejected at every semantic object level; provider/tool/lifecycle commands are not valid contract fields.

identity: itemDigest = sha256(canonical(source snapshot + currentness validators + provenance + content))
resolutionId = sha256(canonical(requirementId + step + status + materialization.id + unresolved))
resolution.normalization: Items are ordered by originating requirement evidence order then rank; provenance and validators are canonicalized by semantic fields before hashing.
resolution.consumability: COMPLETE and PARTIAL are consumable only when every REQUIRED evidence requirement is satisfied; UNSATISFIED is never consumable.
resolution.operationalCounters: consumed.{items,materializedBytes,providerCalls,resolutionSteps} are cumulative budget evidence and excluded from resolutionId.

currentness.requiredCurrent: Exact snapshotRef + at least one STRONG validator.
currentness.rule: Weak/timestamp-only evidence cannot satisfy REQUIRED CURRENT. Strong identity proves representation identity/currentness, not semantic correctness.

progression.next: index = previous.index + 1 and previousResolutionId equals exact prior resolutionId
progression.rule: Immutable snapshots; cumulative consumption never decreases or exceeds original requirement budget.

compatibilityContract.backend: BackendWorkOrder repositoryRef/revision/requiredFiles -> repository EXACT requirements -> ContextResolution -> existing BackendContextSchema with exact repository ref/revision, ordered files and sourceRef.

researchEvidence.finding: Current Backend and QA resolution is explicit pre-worker source IO; sourceRef plus QA producer/acceptance provenance already form compatibility identity evidence.
renderAgentContext already bounds selected prompt blocks by maxBlocks/history/maxSerializedChars; resolution should project into this existing boundary rather than replace it.

Non-turn-aware context renders before strategy/model execution; turn-aware prepareTurn renders each turn, so requirement resolution must be frozen per agent call to avoid hidden turn-to-turn source drift.
Artifact digest/manifest provenance proves identity/currentness constraints but explicitly does not confer semantic correctness or acceptance authority.
Application decides required semantic context and owns orchestration/completion; Oracle resolves/dereferences it before Worker execution.

RFC 9110 distinguishes strong validators from weak validators; strict revision identifiers and collision-resistant representation hashes are examples of strong validation, while modification time can be weak. BB-061 uses this as a currentness model, not as an Oracle wire protocol.

Bazel remote caching separates declared action/input identity from content-addressed output storage; BB-061 applies the same separation between requirement identity and exact materialization/content identity.

MCP keeps resource addressing/reading distinct from tool invocation and carries resource metadata; BB-061 uses this as evidence for source metadata separation, not as a requirement to expose Oracle through MCP.
Aider explicitly fits repository-map context into a token budget; BB-061 keeps bounded materialization as a first-class contract while leaving model-specific token policy above source identity.
Graphiti models temporal validity/currentness-like intervals and provenance-bearing facts; useful evidence that graph providers can stay below a provider-neutral resolution contract.

externalEvidenceSummary.conclusion: No external system is adopted as the BB-061 contract. Evidence supports separation of semantic need from provider mechanics, exact identity from currentness metadata, and bounded projection from source resolution.
